html:
Al-Biruni was a scholar from Khwarazm, south of the Aral Sea, who wrote on astronomy, mathematics, geography, history and India. He is one of the great minds of the medieval Islamic world.

He served local rulers in Khwarazm and northern Iran, and exchanged letters arguing about physics with the young Avicenna. In 1017 Mahmud of Ghazni conquered Khwarazm and took him to Ghazni. Mahmud's raids opened India to him. He learned Sanskrit, talked with Indian scholars, and around 1030 finished his great study of India, described under Al-Biruni's book on India. It tried to describe Hindu beliefs, science and customs fairly, on their own terms.

  • He measured the radius of the Earth by sighting the horizon from a mountain in today's Pakistan; his result was close to the modern figure.
  • He wrote a huge work on astronomy dedicated to Mahmud's son Masud.
  • His Chronology of Ancient Nations compares the calendars of many peoples.
  • He discussed whether the Earth turns on its axis.

He died in Ghazni some time after 1050.
sum: Al-Biruni was a scholar from Khwarazm, south of the Aral Sea, who wrote on astronomy, mathematics, geography, history and India. He is one of the great minds of the medieval Islamic world.
